prompt: A photograph of a marquetry panel in inlaid wood veneers, shot flat from above. The panel shows a lighthouse on a headland with the sea below, the sea cut from a wide piece of wavy-grained veneer running horizontally. Every shape in the picture is a separate piece of wood veneer chosen for its own grain and colour, cut to fit and butted against its neighbours along a fine dark glue line. The shading is done entirely by the direction and figure of the grain and by scorching the edges of pieces in hot sand, which leaves a brown gradient at their borders. There is walnut, pale sycamore, and one piece of burr. The whole panel is under a shellac polish with a few fine scratches in it and one small lifted corner. Shot straight down on a 60mm macro at f8 in soft light angled to bring out the grain and the polish sheen, natural colour.
medium_blurb: Inlaid wood veneer, grain doing the shading.
subject: The panel shows a lighthouse on a headland with the sea below, the sea cut from a wide piece of wavy-grained veneer running horizontally.
